driver: issue #43 (description compression to the amended §3.5 listing-budget target)
method: HOUSECARL_SKILL_AUTHORING §6.5 fan-out, menu variant per houseCARL PR #295: one fresh-context judge per eval query (Opus, HIGH reasoning effort, no tools), each shown ONLY its single query plus the full lettered menu of all 11 NEW descriptions (anonymized, under-test skill unflagged) plus NONE, forced single pick, reasoning before verdict; one Opus adjudicator per skill scored recall/specificity from the judges' reasoning per §6.5 step 4. Judge model deliberately upgraded from PR #295's sonnet-low (maintainer decision). Contamination guard: the live install was moved aside for the fan-out window so fresh judges carried no stale skill listing. Gates: recall >= 80%, specificity >= 50%.
description_measured: Assign Requiem perks to an NPC via houseCARL — derive the source-carried perk set from the actor's gear, spell kit, and tier against Requiem's template ladders, write it as rank-chain PerkPlacements, and disposition a mod's own PERK records, including custom perks that clash with a Requiem crafting or perk gate. Never hand-place Reqtificator-stamped perks — load before writing any Perks list.
adjudicator_notes: No reasoning-vs-token discrepancies; every judge's reasoning matched its verdict token, so no overrides applied. All 10 expect=true rows explicitly weigh H against F (whole-actor NPC) and pick H on a narrow-scope-to-perks argument — the F/H boundary reads as intended. All 10 expect=false rows route away cleanly, and H is named as a near-miss distractor in 9 of them yet rejected each time on a correct distinction: H is an NPC-record PerkPlacements write, not runtime distributor authoring (q13 SPID, q18 SkyPatcher), not new perk design (q12), not player build advice (q14), not a spell-record field (q15), not actor combat-style behavior (q19), not PERK description strings (q20); q11 rejects H as too narrow vs F. 20/20 — no description change indicated.
